deviations.finding: BA spec R13 enumerates 8 stable substrings including `daemon-restart-allow-decoupled`. The implementation uses architectural decoupling (Layer 1.A runs BEFORE the global /allow short-circuit at /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-bash-safety.sh:326 vs :602) instead of emitting this label. As a result, `daemon-restart-allow-decoupled` is never output to stderr.
deviations.rationale: The architectural decoupling-by-ordering provides a STRONGER guarantee than label-based decoupling: daemon-restart commands physically cannot reach the /allow check because Layer 1.A exits 2 before line 602. AC15 (generic /allow does NOT bypass) is satisfied by this ordering. The BA spec R13 list is for stderr-grep stability; missing one label of eight does not weaken the prohibition. If a future cycle wants the label for symmetry with audit logs, a one-line addition suffices.
deviations.recommendation: Optional: add an `echo "BLOCKED: daemon-restart-allow-decoupled"` branch when /allow short-circuit is reached AND command matches daemon-restart pattern. Not blocking.
